cells.tense: Now, and you're the one with your hands on it.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with steady, deliberate care
cells.place: In the clearing where what couldn't hold has just fallen away
cells.ask: Offer someone a plain account of what you've been holding for them — name the cost out loud, once, and let it be received; what comes back is completion you can finally set down, release that feels like arriving instead of quitting.
cells.core: You're tending this on purpose. Two things need you at once and you're holding both — not splitting your weight between them, actually caring for each. The ground just cleared, and instead of grabbing at it you're letting your structure come from attention rather than grip. That's the whole trick: the care is yours, and it isn't costing you the caring.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing landed and you're tending what's left on purpose.

cells.tense: Already braced for a clearing that hasn't come.
cells.verb: Tending what grows with grip instead of care
cells.place: In a clearing you're forcing instead of letting arrive
cells.ask: Let one outcome stay undecided this week — feel your way into the satisfaction of what you've already made before you reach for what's next; when this is in balance, growth happens without forcing, care that doesn't exhaust, and you're holding space instead of clutching it.
cells.core: You're caring for everything ahead of schedule. Before anything has actually fallen apart you've already decided what the clear air will look like, and you're tending each thing against that picture — watering, bracing, re-forming — so the clearing never gets to happen on its own timing. The care is real. It's just been turned into control, and control is starting to exhaust the one doing the caring.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing the clearing instead of letting it come.

cells.tense: Still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.verb: Not tending what grows, because tending stopped
cells.place: Wherever the clearing already happened and you didn't step through
cells.ask: Pick one small thing you've been leaving untended and tend it today, badly — a plant, a message, one person's small need; the strength to keep going comes back from that continued hoping, and what's cultivated reaching completion is what lets your shine return on its own.
cells.core: The structure cleared and you're still standing in the doorway. When it fell, something in you decided you'd been wrong to care for it, so you stopped caring for anything — you just didn't say so. Nothing's been tended since. Growth hasn't stopped wanting to happen; you've stopped wanting to be the one doing it, and that's the hill you're tired on.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing came and you stopped tending.

cells.tense: Pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: Already tending what grows, unseen by yourself
cells.place: In a clearing you keep describing as rubble
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing you've been keeping alive on nothing — call it yours and let it be witnessed by someone else, once; what comes back is the release that flows from completion, surrender that arrives as fulfillment instead of defeat.
cells.core: You're already the one holding this together. The people around you lean on the ground you keep clear; things grow where you decided they should. But when you talk about it, it comes out as if the cleaning happened by itself — as if you just showed up and found things standing. The tending is running. Your name isn't on it, and it's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending this. You just haven't claimed it.
